claims.text: The initial material is equal-atomic NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy.
Laser shock peening at room temperature is an applicable intervention for NbMoTaW.
An LSP intensity of 10^9 W/cm^2 and pulse duration of 10 ns are optimized process conditions for NbMoTaW.
LSP will introduce a high density of dislocations into NbMoTaW.
LSP will introduce residual compressive stresses into NbMoTaW.
The introduced dislocations and compressive stresses will promote dislocation slip.
The introduced dislocations and compressive stresses will promote grain-boundary sliding at room temperature.
Promoting dislocation slip and grain-boundary sliding will enhance the room-temperature ductility of NbMoTaW.
Optimized LSP will improve room-temperature ductility by at least 20% relative to untreated NbMoTaW.
Optimized LSP will maintain the mechanical performance of NbMoTaW at 1600 °C relative to untreated material.
Optimized LSP will not compromise the irradiation resistance of NbMoTaW.
High-density dislocations and residual compressive stresses produced by LSP will enhance irradiation resistance.
Optimization of LSP parameters is crucial for obtaining consistent results.
The exact optimized LSP parameters for NbMoTaW are currently unknown and must be determined.

contradictions.description: The conditions present 10^9 W/cm^2 and 10 ns as optimized parameters, while the uncertainty field says the exact optimized parameters are unknown and still need to be determined.
